site.description: A computational soil microbiology lab at the University of Tromsø. We study how Arctic soil microbiomes respond to permafrost thaw. PI: Dr. Lars Halvorsen. Open data. Reproducible code. Honest uncertainty intervals.
site.author: Halvorsen Lab

props.text: UiT The Arctic University of Norway · Department of Arctic and Marine Biology · Established 2017
We measure how Arctic soil microbiomes respond when the permafrost beneath them thaws — and we publish the data, the code, and the uncertainty.

The Halvorsen Lab is a computational soil microbiology group at the University of Tromsø. We combine long-term field sampling at four established Svalbard and Finnmark sites with whole-metagenome sequencing and Bayesian community-ecology modeling. Our public deliverables are the SoilCast methane-emission posterior, the open MIxC-Arctic 16S/ITS amplicon archive (n=11,847 samples and growing), and reproducible Snakemake pipelines for every published figure. Funded by the Research Council of Norway (project 287912) and a Horizon Europe ERC Consolidator (101090114). Hiring two PhD students for autumn 2026.

content.heading: By the numbers
content.subheading: Updated April 2026. Citation counts pulled from Web of Science; sample counts from the MIxC-Arctic public S3 bucket.

props.text: Permafrost thaw, in the active-layer-deepening regime characteristic of high-Arctic continuous permafrost (mean annual ground temperature −5 °C to −2 °C), restructures soil microbial communities along a methanogenic axis at a rate that current Earth-system models underrepresent by a factor of 1.6 to 2.3 (95% credible interval, Halvorsen et al. 2024, Nature Climate Change). The lab's work since 2024 has focused on closing this gap — both by extending the empirical sampling base and by reformulating the methanogenic-community submodel inside the JULES-permafrost framework.

(1) The MIxC-Arctic time series at Adventdalen (Svalbard, 78°N) shows a 4.1× increase in relative abundance of Methanoflorentaceae across active-layer transects sampled annually 2018–2025 (n=2,847). (2) Stable-isotope probing of duplicate cores incubated at +2 °C confirms these methanogens are metabolically active, not merely present (Halvorsen et al. 2023, ISME Journal). (3) Bayesian state-space modeling of in-situ flux chamber CH₄ data from the same sites (n=4 sites, 18,432 hourly observations) yields a posterior median emission factor 1.9× the JULES-permafrost default (Tan & Halvorsen 2025, Geoscientific Model Development).

The most credible objection is selection bias in our four Svalbard / Finnmark sites — all four are within 12 km of established Forsknings stations, all four are in continental high-Arctic settings, and the maritime mid-Arctic (East Siberian shelf, Northwest Territories) is underrepresented in our archive. Schuur and colleagues (2024, Global Biogeochemical Cycles) argue convincingly that maritime sites show the opposite signal, with marine-derived sulfate suppressing methanogenesis below thaw fronts. We accept this. Our claim is therefore scoped to continental continuous-permafrost regimes and does not generalize to the maritime margin. The lab is in active discussion with the AON-CAP network about cross-site sampling beginning in summer 2027.

What would falsify the central claim: a multi-site replicate sampling effort across continental high-Arctic continuous permafrost showing no shift in Methanoflorentaceae relative abundance under thaw, OR a stable-isotope tracing study demonstrating that the 4.1× abundance shift is not metabolically active. We have pre-registered the analytical pipeline for both tests on OSF (osf.io/halvorsen-lab/mixc-replicate). The replicate sampling effort is the principal aim of ERC Consolidator 101090114 (2024–2029).

props.title: Reframed methanogenic emission factors for continental high-Arctic permafrost: a Bayesian re-analysis of JULES-permafrost outputs.
props.date: Halvorsen, L., Tan, M.-W., Aalto, J., Schuur, E. A. G., & Brodie, E. L. (2025). Nature Climate Change 15, 412–419.
props.tags: Lead claim · Bayesian · JULES-permafrost · Open data · Open code
props.excerpt: We reanalyze JULES-permafrost CH₄ outputs against in-situ flux observations from four continental high-Arctic sites (n=18,432 hourly observations, 2018–2025) and report a posterior median emission factor 1.9× (95% CrI 1.6–2.3) the model default. Implications for CMIP-7 are discussed. Code and data archived at zenodo.org/halvorsen-2025-jules.

props.title: Active methanogen communities in thawing Adventdalen permafrost: a stable-isotope probing time-series, 2018–2023.
props.date: Tan, M.-W., Halvorsen, L., & Mortensen, A. T. (2024). The ISME Journal 18, 1043–1056.
props.tags: Stable isotopes · Methanoflorentaceae · Adventdalen · 6-year time series
props.excerpt: Six annual sampling campaigns at Adventdalen (Svalbard, 78°N) demonstrate that the 4.1× rise in Methanoflorentaceae relative abundance under active-layer deepening reflects metabolically active organisms, not relic DNA. Implications for ¹³C-flux partitioning are quantified.

props.title: MIxC-Arctic: an open 16S/ITS amplicon archive of high-Arctic soil microbiomes (n=11,847 and growing).
props.date: Halvorsen, L., Brodie, E. L., Aalto, J., Mortensen, A. T., et al. (2024). Scientific Data 11, 287.
props.tags: Data descriptor · Open archive · 16S rRNA · ITS · Quarterly updates
props.excerpt: Description of the MIxC-Arctic open archive — sampling protocols, sequencing pipelines, QC procedures, and quarterly-update governance. The archive supersedes the closed-access NMIxC-2019 dataset. All data CC-BY-4.0.

props.title: On the credible interval, not the point estimate: a methodological reply to Schuur et al. (2024).
props.date: Halvorsen, L. & Aalto, J. (2024). Global Biogeochemical Cycles 38, e2024GB008149.
props.tags: Methodological reply · Maritime vs continental · Scope conditions
props.excerpt: We respond to Schuur et al.'s (2024) critique of the Halvorsen et al. (2024) emission-factor estimate. We accept the maritime-site point and re-scope our claim to continental continuous permafrost. The credible interval, not the point estimate, is where the disagreement actually lives.

props.title: Snakemake-permafrost: a reproducible pipeline for amplicon → community → flux modeling on Arctic soils.
props.date: Aalto, J., Mortensen, A. T., & Halvorsen, L. (2024). Methods in Ecology and Evolution 15, 891–903.
props.excerpt: An end-to-end Snakemake pipeline reproducing every figure in the lab's 2022–2024 publications from raw FASTQs through Bayesian community models to flux-coupled emission posteriors. Released under MIT. Containerized on Apptainer.
